value.lineage: Kalman filter (1960, Rudolf Kalman): recursive least-squares estimation of hidden state from noisy measurements via predict/update; this is a minimal scalar C++ reference for embedded sensor smoothing

HUMAN_PROBLEM.value: optimal recursive estimation of hidden state under noise

value.built_to: recover a hidden true value from a stream of noisy measurements by recursively combining a prediction with each new observation, weighted by their uncertainties
value.pressure: measurement noise and the impossibility of observing the true state directly; a naive average lags, a raw reading is jittery
value.success_means: an estimate that tracks the true state with error variance far below the raw measurement noise

value.failure_condition: a mistuned filter either lags reality (over-smooths) or passes the noise through (under-smooths); a navigation estimate drifts and the vehicle mislocates

ANCESTRY.value: Kalman filter (1960, Rudolf Kalman): recursive least-squares estimation of hidden state from noisy measurements via predict/update; this is a minimal scalar C++ reference for embedded sensor smoothing

cut.note: one scalar recursion in five lines; the interesting anatomy is that its 'process noise' term is not the Kalman one: the estimate error grows with the size of the last correction, not with a fixed q per step

provenance.grade_basis: Techne FOSSIL_PACKET.json PROVENANCE_GRADE where issued, else the record's handoff string mapped (populated per R34; Harmonia may re-grade)

organs.mechanism: the gain is the ratio of the current estimate error to the sum of estimate and measurement errors; the estimate moves toward the measurement by K times the innovation; the estimate error shrinks by (1-K)
organs.input: a scalar measurement; the two error magnitudes
assumptions: a random-walk state with no dynamics (no prediction step: the prior is the last estimate)
errors are treated as magnitudes, not variances (no squares anywhere)
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: three multiplications and one division per sample on an 8-bit microcontroller
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: with no process-noise growth the gain decays toward zero and the filter stops tracking; the next organ is the author's fix
organs.source_boundary: the first two statements of updateEstimate

organs.human_name: updateEstimate line 3: err_est = (1-K) err_est + |last - current| * q
organs.mechanism: after shrinking the estimate error by (1-K), the code ADDS q times the absolute change the update just made; a large correction (the signal is moving) inflates the error, which raises the next gain; a quiet signal lets the error and gain decay
assumptions: a big correction means the model was wrong, so trust the next measurement more: an adaptive heuristic standing in for a process-noise variance
organs.fitness_value_in_ancestor: tracks steps without a tuned process model; the whole reason the library is popular
organs.failure_landscape: by reading: the error is driven by the FILTER'S OWN output change, so measurement noise that happens to move the estimate also inflates the error (a positive feedback that the true Kalman recursion does not have); no measurement
organs.human_prior: the author's own device; the Kalman process noise Q is a constant added to the prior variance, not a term proportional to |innovation|
